- **In English:** Haidian town (S05, S1231, S02, S240, S241, S245, S246, S247, S20, S03, S1235, S207, S22, S27)
- **What it was:** a market town outside the garden walls (S05, S1231, S02, S240, S241, S245, S246, S247, S20, S03, S1235, S207, S22, S27 · confidence A)
- **In 1860:** in use; the French marched through it 6 Oct 1860 (S241 p.287; S240 p.224); robbers and dead in its streets late Oct (S240 pp.302-303); a village between the camp and Peking burned in the night of 7-8 Oct, by Chinese according to Varin (S245 p.239; its name not given); 庚申夷氛纪略 (S1235, Nov 1860): the troops 直扑海淀 unopposed on 八月廿二日 (6 Oct); villages outside 西直门 and three other gates 盡遭蹂躏; no source read says the town itself burned (S05, S1231, S02, S240, S241, S245, S246, S247, S20, S03, S1235, S207, S22, S27)
- **Size:** no house or population count found; Varin 1862 p.227: 'On fit deux kilomètres dans le village' (S05, S1231, S02, S240, S241, S245, S246, S247, S20, S03, S1235, S207, S22, S27)
- **Where:** outline = the built-up block of the AMS 1944 sheet (S20) traced by eye, placed with the maps worker's affine (rms 95 m): B for 1944, C for 1860 (the town may have been larger or smaller; Varin p.227 rode 2 km through village along the road); it fits today's old-town streets 海淀南路 to 海淀路, 苏州街 to 中关村大街 (S05, S1231, S02, S240, S241, S245, S246, S247, S20, S03, S1235, S207, S22, S27 · confidence C)
- **Note:** [j76:1b] 西直門外十二里曰海淀淀有南有北; 畅春园 stands at 南海淀 [j76:1a]; 南海淀 six temples incl. 清梵寺, 永通寺 [j99:23a]; 畅春园守备署在海甸莊 [j73:6b]. 天咫偶闻 j9 (1907): 海甸，大鎮也; princes and ministers had gardens, the Hanlin the 澄怀园, the Six Boards' clerks rented temple rooms; eating houses by the river; 士夫居第 in the 灯笼库 quarter; the town street stone-paved (甸鎮街石路). Malone p.35: crossroads on the main street with pailous, a street north to 清梵寺, picture porches at the east end (1713 scroll). d'Hérisson p.300-301: 'ville de peu d'importance', 'une dépendance du palais'. 苏州街 = 萬壽街 from 万寿寺 north to 畅春园 [j77:11a].
